summary: TLS session-ticket truncation by egress TLS-inspection proxy causing resumed-session failures, increased full-handshakes, and CDN rate-limits on model artifact fetches
description: Customer reports intermittent model download failures and elevated artifact 429s coming from their CDN when running Redwood Private behind a corporate TLS-inspection appliance. Failures correlate with spikes in full TLS handshakes from serving nodes: resumed-session attempts are rejected by origin, triggering extra handshakes and hitting upstream CDN rate limits. This appears isolated to the customer's private deployment and began after the customer rolled out an inspection appliance firmware update.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Private deploy in VPC with outbound routed through corporate TLS-inspection appliance (in-line proxy/inspection).
2) Start a batch of model pulls from serving nodes targeting S3-backed presigned URLs via CDN (simulated load: 200 concurrent fetches across 8 nodes).
3) Observe TLS handshakes and attempt session resumption (TLSv1.3) between serving node and CDN/origin.
4) Notice increased 5xx/429 responses and repeated full-handshakes in tcpdump/collector logs when inspection appliance is in inline mode.
logs:
TLS client debug: 'TLSv1.3: session resumption attempted with ticket; server responded: 'error:0A00018A:SSL routines::testrun:session ticket parse failed'
Serving node kernel tcpdump snippet: 'ClientHello (session_ticket ext len=256), ServerHello, ALERT: unexpected_message'
CDN logs: repeated 429 spikes with reason 'rate_limit_full_handshake' (approx 2.3x baseline)
Proxy syslog (inspection appliance): 'tls_ticket_truncation: session_ticket length reduced to 64 due to configured header limit'
investigation_notes:
- Timeline: Issue started 2026-03-09 after customer applied appliance firmware 3.2.1. Prior to that, resume worked normally.
- Captured PCAPs from node-01 and node-03: ClientHello includes session_ticket extension of expected length (~256 bytes). Downstream (after appliance) the session_ticket extension length is truncated to 64 bytes; origin rejects the ticket as malformed and forces a full handshake.
- Appliance vendor confirmed a static buffer-limit in the TLS-inspection engine introduced in 3.2.1 that truncates session-ticket extensions over 128 bytes. Vendor reproduces locally and assigned patch ticket VEND-1452.
- Full-handshake increases total CPU/time on origin side and on CDN edges, triggering edge-side rate limiting for repeated heavy handshakes from same source IP blocks (customer egress NATed behind limited set of EIPs).
- Impact includes: failed artifact downloads (429/503), streaming interruptions (gRPC stream resets) and increased token spend due to KV cache invalidation when nodes reconnect.
comments: Support (Asha): Initial triage - collected tcpdumps and asked customer to move a single node to bypass inspection for test. Customer confirmed bypass node had normal resumption and no 429s.
Customer (Helios NOC): We pushed firmware 3.2.1 widely on 2026-03-09. Rolling back to 3.1.8 on a canary firewall removed the failures. Vendor investigating.

SRE (Diego): Added a temporary mitigation suggestion: configure egress path for serving nodes to use additional public EIPs (reduce NAT coalescing) and reduce concurrent simultaneous fetches during peak, until vendor patch is applied.
Vendor (TLS-appliance): Confirmed bug in 3.2.1 TLS-inspect; hotfix v3.2.1-patch1 scheduled. Reproduction steps provided to customer.
resolution:
Workarounds applied and permanent resolution: 
1) Customer rolled back appliance firmware to 3.1.8 for inline inspection and verified resumed-session success across test nodes. This immediately reduced origin full-handshake rate and cleared CDN 429s.
2) Short-term mitigation: customer added an alternate egress route for serving nodes to go to internet via a different NAT pool (spread EIP footprint) to avoid hitting CDN handshake rate limits caused by NAT coalescing.
3) Vendor released v3.2.1-patch1 on 2026-03-12 which preserves session_ticket extension length; customer to schedule patch during maintenance window. 
4) Redwood added defensive server-side tolerance: runtime now treats 'malformed_ticket' responses as non-fatal and increases retry backoff/outbound concurrency throttle for 24 hours after handshake failures to reduce pressure on CDN edges (github PR linked). 

Follow-ups:
- SRE to add a runbook entry for 'inspection-proxy ticket truncation' under Networking playbooks. (Owner: Diego Morales)
- Customer to provide rollout plan for vendor patch and confirm in ticket once deployed. (Owner: Helios NOC)
- Monitor for recurrence for one week after patch; if reoccurs, escalate to incident with additional telemetry.
next_steps: Customer to apply vendor patch v3.2.1-patch1 during scheduled maintenance and validate resumed-session behavior across all nodes.
Diego to verify Redwood runtime backoff change in staging and schedule hotfix roll to prod if metrics are stable.
Support to keep ticket open until customer confirms patch deployment and 72h of stable artifact fetch success.
